name: What Does Like-for-Like Kitchen Estimate Comparison Mean?

mainEntity.name: What does a like-for-like comparison mean for kitchen remodeling estimates?
mainEntity.text: What does a like-for-like comparison mean for kitchen remodeling estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: A like-for-like comparison means every contractor prices the same finished result. Provide identical plans, measurements, appliance specifications, cabinet layout, countertop material, backsplash area, flooring limits, lighting requirements, plumbing locations, and finish expectations. Ask contractors to confirm assumptions in writing. Compare more than the headline total. Match cabinet construction, hardware, countertop thickness and edge, sink installation, electrical fixtures, plumbing fixtures, flooring preparation, painting, permits, delivery, disposal, cleanup, warranty, and project management. Check whether each bid includes tax, subcontractors, temporary protection, and final inspection corrections. If a line is absent, mark it “not stated” rather than assuming it is included. Ask for a revised proposal or written clarification. Keep allowances separate from fixed prices and identify provisional work. This method is especially useful when comparing a full-service remodeler with a cabinet-focused company or a design-build contractor. The result should be an adjusted expected total for the same scope. Only after that adjustment should schedule, communication, warranty, payment terms, references, and contractor experience influence the decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: A like-for-like comparison matches scope, measurements, materials, product quality, labor, permits, disposal, schedule, warranty, and payment terms across estimates. If one proposal contains different assumptions, revise it before comparing totals. Otherwise, the apparent price difference may reflect missing work rather than lower cost.
